items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own theorem thm:universal-tm at source lines 1434-1443: there is a Turing machine U which on input (e,n) halts exactly when the machine with index e halts on n, and reproduces its output. The proof at source lines 1445-1512 is an outline construction rather than a machine written step by step, and that is how the author presents it (the source explicitly says that producing U is basically impossible and that the outline plus the Church-Turing thesis is what is offered). Its content is a simulation architecture: decode the index e to the right of the input into a list of unary blocks describing the instructions of M_e, write the start state and the number 1 next to that description, copy the input with each stroke replaced by a block of three strokes so that the simulated tape uses a three-symbol alphabet, and then repeat a cycle of steps that reads the simulated tape, finds the matching instruction, rewrites the simulated symbol, updates the recorded state, and moves the recorded head position. Each of those stages is a genuinely different block of machinery, and the last one has to handle the case in which the simulated machine halts, by converting the simulated tape back into a block of strokes. Because the argument is an outline completed by the Church-Turing thesis rather than an explicit machine, it is marked for human spot-check. No result outside the retained text is used beyond the thesis the author invokes.
